The user was planning a road trip from Denver to Mount Rushmore. The user had returned the previous month, in April 2023, from a 4-day family trip to Yellowstone National Park covering a total of 1,200 miles.

The assistant said Denver to Mount Rushmore is about 570 miles and takes 8-9 hours of driving, suggesting I-25 N to I-90 E, then exit 57 for US-16 E, with scenic stops in Cheyenne, Wall Drug in Wall, SD, and Badlands National Park.

The assistant recommended camping near Mount Rushmore at the Mount Rushmore National Memorial KOA (within walking distance), Custer State Park's Sylvan Lake Campground (about 20 miles away), Rushmore RV Resort, American Presidents Resort, Keystone RV Park, Deer Mountain Campground (about 10 miles) and Horsethief Lake Campground (about 15 miles).
The user asked about the amenities, activities and RV rentals at the Mount Rushmore National Memorial KOA, which they were considering as a camping option instead of a hotel.

The assistant said the Mount Rushmore National Memorial KOA has a pool with a water slide, a playground, a convenience store, coin laundry, free Wi-Fi, a fenced dog park, an 18-hole mini golf course, a game room, hiking access to the Presidential Trail, and a seasonal shuttle to the monument.

The assistant listed KOA cabins: Deluxe Cabins with a full kitchen and private bathroom sleeping up to 6, Kamping Kabin with a kitchenette sleeping up to 4, and Tent Cabin sleeping up to 4. It said the KOA also rents RVs including travel trailers, motorhomes and pop-up campers, and gave the phone number (800) 562-1885 for reservations.
The user decided to book the deluxe cabin rental at the Mount Rushmore National Memorial KOA and asked whether its shuttle to the monument is free and how often it runs.

The assistant said the Mount Rushmore National Memorial KOA shuttle runs from late May to early October every 30 minutes from 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM, with the last shuttle leaving the KOA at 5:30 PM, takes 10-15 minutes each way, and is free for KOA guests.
The user said that on the first day of the Yellowstone trip, the family drove around 300 miles to reach Jackson, Wyoming, a long drive that was worth it for the scenic views.
The assistant said the drive from Denver to Jackson passes scenic areas including the Snowy Range and Wind River Canyon, and that Grand Teton National Park lies just north of Jackson.

The assistant recommended Keystone restaurants The Keystone Cafe, The Ruby House Restaurant and The Alpine Inn; Hill City options The Hill City Cafe, The Alpine Slide Restaurant and 1880 Train's Hill City Depot Cafe; and Rapid City options The Independent Ale House, Firehouse Brewing Company and Delmonico Grill.
The assistant also suggested Carver's Cafe near Mount Rushmore and the Custer State Park restaurant at the State Game Lodge, which serves buffalo burgers and bison meatloaf.
The user was planning a road trip from Denver to Aspen, Colorado, and asked for the best route and scenic stops along the way.

The assistant said Denver to Aspen is about 160 miles and takes 3-4 hours via I-70 W and CO-82 E, with scenic detours to Georgetown (about 45 minutes off route), Loveland Pass (about 30 minutes), Copper Mountain (about 20 minutes), Glenwood Springs (about 1 hour) and Maroon Bells (about 1.5 hours).
The user decided to take the scenic route, stopping at Loveland Pass and Copper Mountain, and asked about the road conditions on CO-82 E.

The assistant said CO-82 E in spring can have snow and ice above 9,000 ft, wet and slippery roads, rockfall, and single-lane restrictions, and recommended checking the Colorado Department of Transportation (CDOT) website and mobile app before leaving.
The user said they would check road conditions before leaving, were considering a stop at Maroon Lake, and were unsure whether they had enough time to get there from Aspen.

The assistant said Maroon Lake is about 10 miles southwest of Aspen, a 20-30 minute drive, and that the lake is worth the detour if the user has at least 1-2 hours, including a 1-2 mile hike around the lake.
The user decided to fit Maroon Lake into the trip and asked about parking and shuttle buses.

The assistant said Maroon Lake parking is limited in peak season (June to September): the main lot has about 50-60 spots and often fills by 9-10 am, the Maroon Creek Road lot about 2 miles away has 20-30 spots, and the Aspen Highlands lot about 4 miles away has a free US Forest Service shuttle every 20-30 minutes in peak season.

The user said they had covered a total of 1,800 miles on three recent road trips: a solo trip to Durango, a weekend trip to Breckenridge, and a family trip to Santa Fe, and felt comfortable with the drive and exploring new scenic spots.

The assistant gave photo tips for Maroon Lake, including shooting during golden hour, using the calm water for reflections, using a polarizing filter to reduce glare, bracketing exposures for HDR, and respecting the environment and wildlife.
The user planned to get to Maroon Lake early to catch the golden hour and asked for lunch recommendations in Aspen after the visit.
